After that, go to YouTube and find a morning yoga video that’s right around 20 minutes long, open the actual video page, and tell me the title and duration so I can see whether it feels short enough for a real weekday routine. If that general option seems reasonable, stay on YouTube and specifically check whether Yoga With Adriene has a morning yoga video under 20 minutes that would fit the same need, and confirm from the video page or description whether it’s actually a vinyasa flow style session; please open that in its own tab too so I can compare the two yoga options side by side. To round this out, use Google to find at least three approachable or funny yoga instructors who post free classes on YouTube, and for each one give me the instructor’s name, a channel or website link, and a short note on why they seem especially beginner-friendly compared with the yoga videos you found earlier. In the end, I just want a concise resource list for this morning routine, with the key links, and please keep the math video plus the two yoga video tabs open so I can look at them myself.

Here is your resource list for your weekday morning routine, with the math and yoga video tabs kept open in your browser:

---

### 1. Math Refresher: Arithmetic Sequences (Explicit & Recursive Formulas)
* **Title:** Arithmetic Sequences: Writing Recursive & Explicit Formulas
* **Creator / Channel:** SimpLEEfied
* **Duration:** 11:42
* **Link:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5aPQpVwN_Hc
* **Status:** Open in **Tab ID 2052873310**
* **Notes:** A concise lesson that walks step-by-step through both explicit formulas ($a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d$) and recursive formulas ($a_n = a_{n-1} + d$) with practical sequence examples.

---

### 2. General Morning Yoga (~20 Minutes)
* **Title:** 20 min Full Body Morning Yoga - Stretch & Energize
* **Creator / Channel:** Yoga with Kassandra
* **Duration:** 21:44
* **Link:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ITRvSHLcwis
* **Status:** Open in **Tab ID 2052873311**
* **Notes:** Hits right around the 20-minute mark (21:44) and balances energizing movement with stretches to awaken stiffness without requiring equipment or intense cardio.

---

### 3. Yoga With Adriene Option (<20 Minutes)
* **Title:** Short Wake Up Flow - 15 Minute Morning Yoga
* **Creator / Channel:** Yoga With Adriene
* **Duration:** 13:43
* **Link:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8bEWn2E9uo
* **Status:** Open in **Tab ID 2052873312**
* **Style Confirmation:** **Not a traditional vinyasa flow.** Although the title contains the word "Flow," the description and lesson structure emphasize a gentle, breath-centric wake-up stretch starting seated to reboot mobility and the nervous system. It avoids continuous, athletic vinyasa sequences (like repeated chaturanga/plank transitions), making it lower intensity than a classic vinyasa flow class.

---

### 4. Approachable / Humorous Yoga Instructors with Free YouTube Classes

1. **Yogi Bryan**
   * **Channel / Link:** https://www.youtube.com/@yogi_bryan (Website: https://yogibryan.com/)
   * **Why Beginner-Friendly:** Incorporates lighthearted humor, comedic sketches, and relaxed language to strip away the seriousness and intimidation of yoga. Compared to standard instructor-led flows, Bryan's classes eliminate performance pressure and make showing up on the mat feel casual and fun.

2. **Charlie Follows**
   * **Channel / Link:** https://www.youtube.com/@CharlieFollows (Website: https://charliefollows.com/)
   * **Why Beginner-Friendly:** Focuses on unhurried, gentle pacing with clear, friendly cues and frequent modifications for stiff bodies. Compared to dynamic 20-minute routines like Kassandra's, her classes allow extra time to settle into postures without rushing between transitions.

3. **Jessamyn Stanley**
   * **Channel / Link:** https://www.youtube.com/@JessamynStanley (Website: https://theunderbelly.com/)
   * **Why Beginner-Friendly:** Known for an authentic, funny, and body-positive teaching style. She openly laughs off lost balance and encourages listening to your own body rather than conforming to rigid studio poses, contrasting with more conventional, polished yoga aesthetics.
